hi: अन्नम् (food) = बहु कुर्वीत (one should make abundant / बहुत बनाना चाहिए / अधिक-से-अधिक उत्पन्न करना चाहिए)। वह (तत्) व्रतम् (vow) है। पृथिवी (earth) ही (वा) अन्नम् (food) है। आकाश (space) = अन्नाद (the eater of food)। पृथिवी में (पृथिव्याम्) आकाश (space) प्रतिष्ठित (established) है। आकाश में (आकाशे) पृथिवी प्रतिष्ठित है। इस प्रकार अन्न = अन्न में प्रतिष्ठित। जो इसे जानता है — वह प्रतिष्ठित होता है। अन्नवान् अन्नाद भवति। महान् होता है — प्रजया, पशुभिः, ब्रह्मवर्चसेन, महान् कीर्त्या।
en: One should make food abundant (annaṁ bahu kurvīta). That is the vow. Earth (pṛthivī) is food. Space (ākāśa) is the eater of food. In earth, space is established. In space, earth is established. Thus food is established in food. He who knows this — that food is established in food — becomes established. He becomes possessing food and an eater of food. He becomes great — in offspring, cattle, the radiance of sacred knowledge, great in fame.

ws.h: बहुत बनाना चाहिए / one should make abundant / increase
ws.e: one should make abundant / one should increase — bahu (much/many) + kurvīta (optative of √kṛ, to do/make); the third food-vow: PRODUCE abundance — grow food, share food, multiply food; this goes beyond personal attitude (don't despise) and personal action (don't refuse) to SOCIAL responsibility — ensure abundance for all

ws.h: पृथिवी / भूमि / earth
ws.e: earth — the element; here earth = food because earth produces all food — plants grow from earth, animals eat plants; earth is the ultimate source of all physical nourishment

ws.h: आकाश / space / ether
ws.e: space / ether — the subtlest of the five elements; here space = the 'eater' of earth — space contains earth (earth floats in space), and in the dissolution of the universe, earth returns to space; yet space is also 'in' earth (every atom contains space within it)

gr: The third food-vow — make food abundant: the most socially oriented of the three vows. The vow: 'annaṁ bahu kurvīta — tat vratam' — 'One should make food abundant — that is the vow.' This is remarkable: the Taittirīya makes PRODUCING FOOD a sacred duty — a vrata (vow). Not just eating reverently or accepting gratefully, but actively INCREASING the supply of food. This is a social and ecological teaching embedded in a spiritual text. The cosmic elements: earth (pṛthivī) = food, space (ākāśa) = the eater. Earth and space are interdependent: earth exists IN space (space contains earth), and space exists IN earth (every object contains internal space — the space between atoms, the hollows within things). The most solid (earth) and the most subtle (space) support each other. The complete food-ethics: the three vows together form a complete food-ethics: (1) Don't despise food (inner attitude). (2) Don't refuse/waste food (personal action). (3) Make food abundant (social responsibility). Together: reverence + acceptance + generosity = the complete anna-dharma (food-ethics).
mt: REVIEW_NEEDED: taittiriya_upanishad_3.9.1 — The third food-vow ('annaṁ bahu kurvīta') is perhaps the most socially significant teaching in the Upanishads — it makes food-production a sacred obligation. This connects directly to the Taittirīya's overall theme of integrating spiritual knowledge with material life. The earth-space pair represents the extreme ends of the element spectrum — pṛthivī (the grossest) and ākāśa (the subtlest). Their mutual dependence (earth IN space, space IN earth) is both cosmologically true and phenomenologically observable: everything exists in space, and space exists within everything. The three food-vows together — 'na nindyāt' (don't despise), 'na paricakṣīta' (don't reject), 'bahu kurvīta' (make abundant) — form a progressive sequence from inner attitude to outer social action: reverence → acceptance → generosity.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'बहु कुर्वीत' = अन्न-उत्पादन = धर्म — अन्न = ब्रह्म — अतः अन्न बढ़ाना = ब्रह्म-सेवा। पृथिवी-आकाश = स्थूलतम-सूक्ष्मतम = परस्पर-आश्रित। तीन व्रत = अन्न-धर्म (food-ethics) का सम्पूर्ण ढाँचा।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'bahu kurvīta' = food-production = dharma — food = Brahman — therefore increasing food = serving Brahman. Earth-space = grossest-subtlest = interdependent. Three vows = the complete framework of food-ethics.
advaita.ins: Make food abundant — that's the vow. If food is Brahman, then producing, sharing, and multiplying food is sacred service. Earth supports space; space contains earth. The grossest and subtlest depend on each other. Three vows: revere it, accept it, multiply it.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'बहु कुर्वीत' = भगवान् का अन्न-रूप = सबको देना (sharing) = भगवत्-सेवा (service to God)। पृथिवी = भगवान् का आधार-रूप (God as foundation)। आकाश = भगवान् का विस्तार-रूप (God as expansion)। अन्न बढ़ाना = भगवान् की सेवा।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'bahu kurvīta' = God's food-form = sharing with all = service to God. Earth = God as foundation. Space = God as expansion. Increasing food = serving God.
vishisht.ins: Make food abundant — share it, grow it, multiply it. Food is God's form, and sharing food is serving God. Earth is God's foundation; space is God's embrace. The one who produces food for others participates in God's sustaining work.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'बहु कुर्वीत' = भौतिक समृद्धि (material abundance) = आध्यात्मिक कर्तव्य (spiritual duty)। पृथिवी-आकाश = स्थूल-सूक्ष्म = एक ही चेतना के दो ध्रुव। अन्न-उत्पादन = चेतना का भौतिक स्तर पर कार्य।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'bahu kurvīta' = material abundance = a spiritual duty. Earth-space = gross-subtle = two poles of one consciousness. Food-production = consciousness working at the physical level.
aurobindo.ins: Producing abundance is a spiritual act. Earth and space — the densest and subtlest — are two faces of the same consciousness. Making food abundant means consciousness working through you at the material level. The spiritual life includes caring for the physical needs of all.

dp.q: 🔍 The three food-vows — a complete ethics of nourishment
dp.a: The three food-vows of the Bhṛguvallī form a complete ethics of nourishment — progressing from inner attitude to social responsibility: Vow 1: 'Annaṁ na nindyāt' (Don't despise food) — INNER ATTITUDE. This addresses the mind: cultivate reverence for food. Don't hold physical nourishment in contempt. Don't privilege the 'spiritual' over the 'material.' Food is Brahman's first face — treat it with the respect due to the sacred. Vow 2: 'Annaṁ na paricakṣīta' (Don't reject food) — PERSONAL ACTION. This addresses behaviour: accept food when offered. Don't waste food. Don't be fastidious or squeamish about nourishment. Receive what life offers with gratitude. Vow 3: 'Annaṁ bahu kurvīta' (Make food abundant) — SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY. This addresses the community: produce food, share food, ensure abundance for all. This is the most outward-facing vow — it transforms spiritual insight into social action. The progressive structure: (a) Inner → outer: from thought (don't despise) to action (don't refuse) to service (make abundant). (b) Individual → collective: from personal attitude to personal behaviour to social responsibility. (c) Passive → active: from not-despising (passive) to not-refusing (responsive) to actively-producing (creative). The integration: together, the three vows integrate Bhrigu's highest realisation (ānanda = Brahman) with the humblest daily reality (food). The sage who knows Brahman as bliss does not withdraw from the world — they engage with the world's most basic need (food) with reverence, acceptance, and generosity. This is the Taittirīya's distinctive teaching: spirituality is not escape from matter but transformation of matter through knowledge.

dp.q: 🔍 Earth and space — the grossest and subtlest support each other
dp.a: The third vow meditates on earth (pṛthivī) and space (ākāśa) — the two extremes of the element spectrum: Earth = the grossest element: solid, tangible, heavy, stable. Earth is the element of FORM — it gives things shape, weight, and location. In the creation sequence, earth is the last element to emerge (ātman → ākāśa → vāyu → agni → āpaḥ → pṛthivī) — the most condensed, most material expression of Brahman. Space = the subtlest element: invisible, intangible, weightless, boundless. Space is the element of POSSIBILITY — it gives things room to exist. In the creation sequence, space is the FIRST element to emerge — the most immediate, most subtle expression of Brahman. Their mutual dependence: (a) Earth is 'in' space — the earth floats in space; space contains, surrounds, and pervades the earth. Without space, earth would have nowhere to be. (b) Space is 'in' earth — every object contains internal space; atoms are mostly empty space; the earth itself is riddled with caves, hollows, pores. Without earth, space would have nothing to pervade. The teaching: the subtlest and the grossest are not separate — they interpenetrate. The most material (earth/food) and the most spiritual (space/ākāśa) support each other. This is the Taittirīya's answer to false asceticism: you cannot have the spiritual without the material, or the material without the spiritual. They are food established in food.

hi: किसी को भी (न कञ्चन) वसतौ (at one's dwelling / निवास पर) प्रत्याचक्षीत (one should not turn away / लौटाना नहीं चाहिए) — यह (तत्) व्रतम् (vow / व्रत) है। इसलिए (तस्मात्) जिस किसी भी (यया कया च) विधि (method) से बहु (abundant) अन्न (food) प्राप्नुयात् (one should procure / प्राप्त करे)। 'इसके लिए अन्न तैयार किया गया है (अराध्य अस्मा अन्नम्)' इति आचक्षते (they say)। यह (एतत्) मुखतः (in the beginning / from the front / प्रारम्भ से) अन्न राद्धम् (food prepared / अन्न तैयार किया गया) — मुखतः (in the beginning) उसके लिए अन्न राध्यते (food is prepared / तैयार होता है)। मध्यतः (in the middle) अन्न राद्धम् — मध्यतः उसके लिए अन्न राध्यते। अन्ततः (in the end) अन्न राद्धम् — अन्ततः उसके लिए अन्न राध्यते। जो (यः) इस प्रकार (एवम्) जानता है (वेद): [ब्रह्म] = क्षेम (security / सुरक्षा) इति = वाणी (speech) में। श्री (prosperity) और योगक्षेम (attainment and security) = प्राण-अपान (inhalation-exhalation) में। कर्म (action) = हाथों (hands) में। गति (movement) = पैरों (feet) में। विमुक्ति (release) = पायु (excretory organ) में। ये (इति) मानुषी (human) समाज्ञाः (recognitions / perceptions / पहचान) हैं। अब (अथ) दैवी (divine / दिव्य): तृप्ति (satisfaction) = वृष्टि (rain) में। बल (strength) = विद्युत् (lightning) में। यशः (fame) = पशुओं (cattle) में। ज्योतिः (light) = नक्षत्रों (stars) में। प्रजाति (procreation), अमृतम् (immortality), आनन्दः (bliss) = उपस्थ (organ of generation) में। सर्वम् (everything) = आकाश (space) में। उसे (तत्) प्रतिष्ठा (support) इति उपासीत (one should meditate) — प्रतिष्ठावान् (well-established) भवति। तत् महः इति उपासीत — महावान् भवति। तत् मनः (mind) इति उपासीत — मानवान् (endowed with understanding) भवति। तत् नमः (reverence) इति उपासीत — नम्यन्ते (bow down / झुकती हैं) अस्मै (to him) कामाः (desires)। तत् ब्रह्म इति उपासीत — ब्रह्मवान् भवति। तत् ब्रह्मणः परिमर (the dying around Brahman / ब्रह्म के चारों ओर मरने वाले = ब्रह्म को छोड़कर सब नश्वर) इति उपासीत — उसके चारों ओर (परि) शत्रु (द्विषन्तः) और सपत्न (rivals) म्रियन्ते (die / मरते हैं) — और जो (ये) उसके प्रियजनों (priya) से द्वेष (hatred) करते हैं [वे भी]। वह (सः) जो (यः) इस (अयम्) पुरुष (person) में [है] और (च) जो (यः) उस (असौ) आदित्य (sun) में [है] — वह (सः) एक (ekaḥ) ही है। उस इस प्रकार जानने वाले (एवं विदुषः) के — इस लोक से प्रेत्य (departing / गमन कर) — इस अन्नमय आत्मा को उपसंक्रम्य (having traversed / पार कर), प्राणमय आत्मा को पार कर, मनोमय आत्मा को पार कर, विज्ञानमय आत्मा को पार कर, आनन्दमय आत्मा को प्राप्त कर — इन (इमान्) सभी लोकों (worlds) में कामान्नी (eating food at will / इच्छानुसार अन्न भक्षण करते हुए), कामरूपी (assuming forms at will / इच्छानुसार रूप धारण करते हुए) अनुसंचरन् (wandering / विचरते हुए) — यह (एतत्) साम (Sāma chant) गाता हुआ (गायन्) आस्ते (sits / बैठता है): 'हा ३ वु, हा ३ वु, हा ३ वु! अहम् अन्नम् अहम् अन्नम् अहम् अन्नम् — मैं अन्न हूँ! मैं अन्न हूँ! मैं अन्न हूँ! अहम् अन्नादः अहम् अन्नादः अहम् अन्नादः — मैं अन्न-भक्षक हूँ! अहं श्लोककृत् — मैं श्लोक-कर्ता (maker of verses / śloka-maker) हूँ! अहम् अस्मि प्रथमजा ऋतस्य — मैं ऋत (cosmic order) का प्रथमजन्मा (first-born) हूँ — देवताओं से भी पूर्व (before the gods)। अमृतस्य नाभायि — मैं अमृत (immortality) का नाभि-केन्द्र (navel-centre) हूँ। यो मा ददाति स इदेव माऽवाः — जो मुझे देता है वही मेरा रक्षक (protector) है। अहम् अन्नम् अन्नम् अदन्तम् आद्मि — मैं अन्न हूँ — अन्न को खाने वाले को [भी] मैं खाता हूँ। अहं विश्वं भुवनम् अभ्यभवाम् — मैंने विश्व (universe) को — सम्पूर्ण भुवन (all worlds) को — अभिभूत (pervaded / overcome) कर लिया। सुवर्ण ज्योतीः — मैं सूर्य-समान ज्योतिः (golden light) हूँ।' जो इस प्रकार जानता है — इति उपनिषत् (this is the secret teaching / यह उपनिषद् / रहस्य-विद्या है)।
en: One should never turn away anyone seeking shelter/food at one's dwelling (na kañcana vasatau pratyācakṣīta). That is the vow. Therefore, by whatever means (yayā kayā ca vidhayā), one should procure abundant food. 'Food has been prepared for him' — they say. If food is prepared well from the beginning (mukhataḥ), food is prepared for him from the beginning. If prepared moderately in the middle (madhyataḥ), food is prepared for him moderately. If prepared minimally at the end (antataḥ), food comes to him minimally. He who knows thus: [Brahman is] security (kṣema) in speech; prosperity and security (yoga-kṣema) in prāṇa and apāna; action (karma) in the hands; movement (gati) in the feet; release (vimukti) in the excretory organ — these are the human recognitions (mānuṣīḥ samājñāḥ). Now the divine: satisfaction (tṛpti) in rain; strength (bala) in lightning; fame (yaśas) in cattle; light (jyoti) in the stars; procreation, immortality, and bliss (prajāti, amṛta, ānanda) in the organ of generation; everything (sarva) in space (ākāśa). One should meditate on That as support (pratiṣṭhā) — one becomes well-supported. As greatness (mahas) — one becomes great. As mind (manas) — one becomes thoughtful. As reverence (namas) — desires bow down to him. As Brahman — one becomes possessed of Brahman. As 'that around which all perishes' (parimara) — his enemies and rivals perish around him. He who is in this person (puruṣa) and He who is in that sun (āditya) — He is ONE (ekaḥ). For one who knows thus — departing from this world, having traversed this self made of food, having traversed the self made of breath, having traversed the self made of mind, having traversed the self made of knowledge, having traversed the self made of bliss — wandering through these worlds, eating food at will (kāma-annī), assuming forms at will (kāma-rūpī) — he sits singing this Sāma: 'Hā vu! Hā vu! Hā vu! I am food! I am food! I am food! I am the eater of food! I am the eater of food! I am the eater of food! I am the maker of verses! I am the first-born of the cosmic order (ṛta) — before the gods! I am the navel-centre of immortality! He who gives me — he alone protects me! I am food — I eat the eater of food! I have pervaded the entire universe! I am golden light (suvarṇa jyotiḥ)!' He who knows thus — this is the Upanishad (iti upaniṣat).

ws.s: न कञ्चन वसतौ प्रत्याचक्षीत (na kañcana vasatau pratyācakṣīta)
ws.h: किसी को भी निवास पर से नहीं लौटाना चाहिए / never turn anyone away from your dwelling
ws.e: never turn anyone away from your dwelling — na (not) + kañcana (anyone) + vasatau (at the dwelling/home) + pratyācakṣīta (turn away/refuse); the fourth and most comprehensive food-vow: HOSPITALITY — never refuse food or shelter to anyone who comes to your home; this makes food-sharing an unconditional sacred duty

ws.h: इच्छानुसार अन्न भक्षण करने वाला, इच्छानुसार रूप धारण करने वाला / eating food at will, assuming forms at will
ws.e: eating food at will + assuming forms at will — kāma (desire/will) + annī (eating food) + rūpī (having form); the liberated soul moves freely through all worlds, taking whatever form and nourishment it wills — this is the Vedic description of mokṣa (liberation): complete freedom from limitation

ws.h: मैं अन्न हूँ / I am food
ws.e: I am food — the climactic declaration: the liberated soul identifies with BOTH sides of the food-cycle: 'I am food' (I am the nourishment of all) AND 'I am the eater of food' (I consume and transform all). This collapses the duality of eater and eaten, consumer and consumed — everything is the Self

ws.h: यह उपनिषद् है / this is the secret teaching
ws.e: this is the Upanishad / the secret teaching — the formal closing formula; upaniṣat = the esoteric, liberating teaching; this phrase marks the end of the entire Taittirīya Upanishad — all three Vallīs are concluded with this declaration that what has been taught is the supreme secret knowledge

gr: The grand finale — hospitality, cosmic identification, and the ecstatic song of liberation: this extraordinary concluding mantra weaves together hospitality, cosmic meditation, the identity of the inner self with the cosmic Self, the traversal of the five sheaths, and the ecstatic Sāma-song of the liberated soul. The fourth vow — universal hospitality: 'na kañcana vasatau pratyācakṣīta' — never turn ANYONE away from your home. This is the supreme food-vow: unconditional hospitality. Not just 'don't despise food' or 'don't waste food' but 'share food with everyone who comes.' This is the Vedic atithi-dharma (duty of hospitality) elevated to a sacred vow. The principle of reciprocity: 'arādhyasma annam' — food has been prepared for the giver. The quality of what you give determines what you receive: give generously at the beginning (mukhataḥ), and abundance comes to you from the beginning; give minimally at the end (antataḥ), and only minimal returns come. The cosmic recognitions: Brahman is recognised in every aspect of human and divine life — in speech (security), in breath (prosperity), in hands (action), in feet (movement), in the excretory organ (release); and in the divine realm — in rain (satisfaction), in lightning (strength), in cattle (fame), in stars (light), in the generative organ (procreation, immortality, bliss), in space (everything). The six meditations: meditate on That as support (pratiṣṭhā), greatness (mahas), mind (manas), reverence (namas), Brahman, and as that around which all perishes (parimara). The identity declaration: 'He who is in this person and He who is in that sun — He is ONE.' The inner Self and the cosmic Self are identical — the Taittirīya's version of the mahāvākya. The five-sheath traversal: the liberated soul, departing, traverses each sheath — annamaya → prāṇamaya → manomaya → vijñānamaya → ānandamaya — moving from the outer to the inner, from the gross to the subtle. The Sāma-song of liberation: the ecstatic song — 'Hā vu! I am food! I am food! I am food! I am the eater of food! I am the maker of verses! I am the first-born of ṛta! I am the navel of immortality! I am food — I eat the eater of food! I have pervaded the entire universe! I am golden light!' This is the voice of the Self that has transcended ALL five sheaths and identified with EVERYTHING — food AND eater, individual AND cosmos, mortal AND immortal. 'Iti upaniṣat': 'This is the secret teaching' — the formal conclusion of the entire Taittirīya Upanishad.
mt: REVIEW_NEEDED: taittiriya_upanishad_3.10.1 — This is the longest and most complex mantra in the Bhṛguvallī, serving as the grand conclusion of the entire Taittirīya Upanishad. The fourth vow ('na kañcana vasatau pratyācakṣīta') elevates hospitality to the level of spiritual practice — the Chāndogya (4.1-3) similarly makes feeding guests a form of sacred fire-tending. The identity statement ('sa yaścāyaṁ puruṣe yaścāsāvāditye sa ekaḥ') echoes the Īśa (15-16) where the seeker asks the sun to reveal the truth beneath its golden disc. The five-sheath traversal (upasaṁkramya) describes liberation as a journey THROUGH the five kośas — not rejecting them but passing through them to reach the ānandamaya. The Sāma-song ('aham annam, aham annam, aham annam') is widely cited as one of the most powerful expressions of non-dual realisation in the Upanishads — the liberated soul identifies with BOTH sides of every duality: food AND eater, mortal AND immortal, individual AND cosmos. The triple repetition (3×3) is a Sāma-style chant pattern. The phrase 'aham annam annam adantam ādmi' (I am food, I eat the eater of food) completes the circle begun in the Brahmānandavallī's 'adyate atti ca' — the food that eats and is eaten is now recognised as the Self. 'Iti upaniṣat' closes not just the Bhṛguvallī but the entire Taittirīya Upanishad.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'अहमन्नम्' = आत्मा = सर्वम् (everything) — अन्न भी, अन्नाद भी। पञ्च-कोश-भेदन (traversal of five sheaths) = अध्यास-निवृत्ति (removal of superimposition) — प्रत्येक कोश = 'नेति' (not this) — अन्तिम आत्मा = आनन्दमय के परे = ब्रह्म। 'स एकः' = आत्मा-ब्रह्म-ऐक्य (identity of Self and Brahman) = अद्वैत का सार।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'aham annam' = the Self = everything — food as well as the eater. Traversal of five sheaths = removal of superimposition — each sheath = 'not this' — the final Self = beyond even the ānandamaya = Brahman. 'Sa ekaḥ' = identity of Self and Brahman = the essence of Advaita.
advaita.ins: The ultimate declaration: I am food, I am the eater, I am everything. The liberated soul passes through all five sheaths — food, breath, mind, knowledge, bliss — and discovers the Self that is identical with Brahman. The person within you and the light in the sun are ONE. This is the secret teaching.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'अहमन्नम्' = जीव (soul) = भगवान् के शरीर का अंश — 'स एकः' = भगवान् = सर्वान्तर-आत्मा (innermost Self of all) — पुरुष में भी, आदित्य में भी = एक ही भगवान्। मुक्ति = भगवद्-प्राप्ति (attainment of God) — पञ्च कोशों को पार कर भगवान् तक पहुँचना।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'aham annam' = the soul = part of God's body — 'sa ekaḥ' = God = the innermost Self of all — in person and sun = one God. Liberation = attainment of God — traversing the five sheaths to reach God.
vishisht.ins: The soul discovers its true nature: part of God's body, sustained by God, returning to God. The light in the person and the light in the sun are one God. Liberation is the journey through all five sheaths to find God at the core — and then to wander freely through all worlds, singing the song of unity.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'अहमन्नम्' = चेतना = सब कुछ — अन्न भी, अन्नाद भी, श्लोककृत् भी। 'स एकः' = व्यक्ति में चेतना = ब्रह्माण्ड में चेतना = एक। पञ्च-कोश = चेतना के पाँच स्तर — भौतिक से आनन्द तक — सबको पार कर = पूर्ण चेतना (integral consciousness)। 'सुवर्ण ज्योतीः' = स्वर्णिम प्रकाश = सत्-चित्-आनन्द।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'aham annam' = consciousness = everything — food, eater, and poet. 'Sa ekaḥ' = consciousness in the person = consciousness in the cosmos = one. Five sheaths = five planes of consciousness — from physical to bliss — traversing all = integral consciousness. 'Suvarṇa jyotīḥ' = golden light = Sat-Chit-Ananda.
aurobindo.ins: The final vision: I am everything — food and eater, mortal and immortal, person and cosmos. Consciousness discovers its unity across all planes — physical, vital, mental, knowledge, bliss. The golden light is Sat-Chit-Ananda — the divine radiance that is the nature of all existence. This is the secret teaching.

dp.q: 🔍 'Aham annam' — the ecstatic song of non-dual realisation
dp.a: The concluding Sāma-song — 'aham annam, aham annam, aham annam' (I am food, I am food, I am food) — is one of the most powerful expressions of non-dual realisation in the Upanishads: The triple identity: (1) 'Aham annam' — I am food. The Self identifies with the nourishment of all beings. (2) 'Aham annādaḥ' — I am the eater of food. The Self identifies with all beings that eat. (3) 'Ahaṁ ślokakṛt' — I am the maker of verses. The Self identifies with creative expression, with consciousness that articulates reality. The cosmic claims: (a) 'Aham asmi prathamajā ṛtasya' — I am the first-born of cosmic order (ṛta). The Self precedes the gods — it is the first expression of the universal law. (b) 'Pūrvaṁ devebhyo amṛtasya nābhāyi' — before the gods, I am the navel-centre of immortality. The Self is the HUB of the immortal — the point from which all immortal beings radiate. (c) 'Aham annam annam adantam ādmi' — I am food; I eat the eater of food. The ultimate collapse of the eater-eaten duality: the Self IS food, and the Self CONSUMES those who consume food. Nothing is outside the Self. (d) 'Ahaṁ viśvaṁ bhuvanam abhyabhavām' — I have pervaded/overcome the entire universe. The Self is not limited to one body or one world — it encompasses ALL worlds. (e) 'Suvarṇa jyotīḥ' — I am golden light. The Self's nature is luminous — the golden light of the sun, the radiance of consciousness. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka echo: this song closely parallels BU 1.4.6-10, where the Self realises 'ahaṁ brahmāsmi' (I am Brahman) and 'aham annam, aham annādaḥ' (I am food, I am the eater). The Taittirīya adds the Sāma-chant element — the triple 'hā vu' exclamation — giving it a musical, ecstatic quality.

dp.q: 🔍 'Iti upaniṣat' — the secret teaching completed
dp.a: The Taittirīya Upanishad closes with the formula 'iti upaniṣat' (this is the Upanishad / this is the secret teaching), marking the completion of the entire teaching: What has been taught: across three Vallīs, the Taittirīya has offered: (a) Śikṣāvallī (Valli 1): preparation — phonetics, meditation on OM, the vyāhṛtis, and the convocation address (practical ethics and spiritual readiness). (b) Brahmānandavallī (Valli 2): theory — the definition of Brahman ('satyaṁ jñānam anantam'), the five-sheath analysis, the bliss-calculus, and the declarations on Brahman's creation, entry, and identity with all things. (c) Bhṛguvallī (Valli 3): practice — Bhrigu's five-fold discovery (anna → prāṇa → manas → vijñāna → ānanda), the food-vows, and the ecstatic song of liberation. The three-fold pedagogy: preparation (how to learn) → theory (what to learn) → practice (how to realise). This is a complete curriculum: the Śikṣāvallī prepares the student; the Brahmānandavallī teaches the doctrine; the Bhṛguvallī shows how to DISCOVER the doctrine for oneself. The unity of the three Vallīs: the Śikṣāvallī's teacher says 'svādhyāya-pravacane ca' (study and teaching are the highest tapas). The Brahmānandavallī declares 'satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma' and analyses the five sheaths. The Bhṛguvallī's student REDISCOVERS the five sheaths through tapas and arrives at ānanda. The final song unifies everything: food, eater, cosmic order, immortality, all worlds, golden light — the Self is ALL. 'Iti upaniṣat': this is the secret teaching — secret not because it is hidden but because it can only be known through direct experience. You can HEAR these words, but you can only KNOW their meaning through tapas — through the Bhrigu-method of sustained inquiry and self-discovery.
